in_text_mentions: The patient was diagnosed with acute decompensated heart failure secondary to thyro‐cardiac disease precipitated by atrial fibrillation and anemia. Upper gastrointestinal endoscopy revealed esophageal webs and significantly reduced esophageal motility (Figure 1), raising suspicion for Plummer‐Vinson syndrome. A barium swallow showed focal esophageal dilatation with an incomplete linear filling defect caused by the esophageal webs (Figure 2).
